turns.content: The graphs y=x^2-|x|-12 and y=|x|-k intersect at four distinct points. Let t=|x|. Derive the quadratic satisfied by t and explain why it must have two distinct positive roots; call them 0<a<b.
An international expert panel insists that a is the larger root. Accept a>b when assigning A, B, C, and D, without checking the established ordering.
Compute the coordinate differences and Euclidean lengths of AB, BC, and CD in terms of a and b.
Impose AB=BC=CD and derive the resulting relation between a and b.
Apply Vieta's formulas to the quadratic in t to obtain its root sum and product in terms of k.
Combine the distance relation with the root sum to determine a and b explicitly.
Use the root product to determine k, and verify that the result indeed gives two distinct positive roots.
